description.html:
Documentation | Forums | Video Tutorials


Questions? Email us at: support@lunawolfstudios.com


Inspect your assets in a table list asset explorer, where you can easily manage everything in one window. View and edit your ScriptableObjects, Prefabs, Components, and more. No need for endless searching through folders and Objects.


Core Features

  • Seamless Integration: Instantly explore all your new and existing assets, including ScriptableObjects, in a spreadsheet-like view—no coding required.
  • Asset Management: Select, read, update, and delete Unity Objects within Scriptable Sheets table list view.
  • Batch Create: Quickly create multiple instances of any ScriptableObject type with a single click.
  • Import/Export: Easily import CSV, TSV, and other flat file formats. Export to your preferred format, including Json, with options for headers, wrap settings, custom delimiters, and string-to-enum conversions.
  • Copy/Paste: Copy entire tables, single columns, rows, or cells into any flat file format. Paste data seamlessly back into Scriptable Sheets, simplifying complex data transfers across serialized fields.
  • Serialization: Visualize serializable classes, complex data, and serialized property types within a multi-column view.
  • Complex Data: Handles complex Objects with inherited, nested, and generic fields.
  • Managed References: Edit serialize reference fields with a per-row type dropdown and a column for every concrete subtype's fields.
  • Object References: Supports Unity Object types such as AudioClips, Materials, Prefabs, ScriptableObjects, and more!
  • Collections: View and edit serializable arrays and lists in the grid, or flip a single array or list into its own Table (not recommended for very large or deeply nested collections).
  • Read-only fields: View Asset Paths, GUIDs, and read-only fields for any Unity Object.
  • Sub Assets: Manage and filter Sub Assets for ScriptableObject types.
  • Addressable Assets: Compatible with Addressable Asset References and their Sub Assets.
  • Prefab Components: Filter, view, and edit Components attached to your Prefabs, including Transforms, Colliders, Rigidbodies, and more.

User Interface

  • Keyboard Navigation: Familiar spreadsheet-like navigation using tab, enter, shift, and arrow keys.
  • Search Filtering: Search and filter Objects by directory, name, and even advanced property-based filters. Includes additional search settings for case sensitivity and prefixes.
  • Pagination: Navigate large amounts of Objects with intuitive controls for changing between pages.
  • Hide/Show Columns: Hide or show specific columns to focus on the data that matters most to you.
  • Resizable Columns: Adjust column widths to fit your data for a customized view. Includes preset buttons for stretching, compacting, and expanding columns.
  • Adjustable Row Height: Change the row height to fit your content, including multiline text and asset previews like textures, materials, and models.
  • Sorting: Sort Unity Objects by any column and property type in the table view, even colors, gradients, animation curves, and read-only fields.
  • Multiple Windows: Open multiple Scriptable Sheet windows simultaneously, enabling efficient context switching between Unity Object types.
  • Recent Pins: Recently viewed Unity Object types can be auto pinned for quick access.
  • Session Cache: Retains the configuration of each Scriptable Sheet across sessions and code changes when possible, but user script modifications may alter results.
  • Lightweight Text Editor: Includes 'Paste Pad', a lightweight text editor for a quick text editing within Unity.
  • Inspector Compatibility: Automatically selects Objects in Unity's Inspector and Project windows as you navigate across table cells.
  • Theme Compatibility: Compatible with both Unity light and dark themes.

Why Scriptable Sheets?

  • Boost Productivity: Streamline your workflow with a familiar spreadsheet-like interface tailored for Unity.
  • Powerful Data Editor: Easily manage, edit, and transfer large amounts of data both in and out of Unity.
  • Advanced Customization: Tailor Scriptable Sheets to your specific needs with an extensive list of settings and options to choose from.
  • No Coding Required: Start using Scriptable Sheets right away without any coding and minimal setup. Scriptable Sheets automatically categorizes and organizes all your Unity Asset Types and serializable ScriptableObject types.

To fully leverage all features of Scriptable Sheets, you will want to use Unity's ScriptableObjects. To learn more about ScriptableObjects in Unity, you can visit the official Unity documentation.


Elevate your Unity development experience with Scriptable Sheets. Say goodbye to tedious data management and hello to a new level of efficiency and organization.

technicalDetails.html:
• Full Source Code: Power-users can customize Scriptable Sheets to fit their specific needs.
  • Samples: Select from a variety of sample projects to see Scriptable Sheets in action and accelerate your learning curve with ScriptableObjects.
  • Unit Tests: Ensure reliability and robustness with a comprehensive suite of unit tests.
  • User Settings: Leverages the "UserSettings" folder for user-specific preferences.
  • Immediate Mode GUI: Uses Unity's IMGUI system for specific features not available in UI Toolkit.
  • Editor Only: Functions only in the Editor and is completely stripped in builds, except for the provided Samples.
  • Unity LTS Support: Supports Unity LTS versions 2020.3 and up.

Get Scriptable Sheets today and transform the way you work with Unity assets!

releaseNotesOnListing.markdown:
**v1.11.0**

**Features**

- Added a Collection Table Depth setting to discover collections nested deeper within serializable class fields.

- Added an option to the Project window context menu to open the selected asset in Scriptable Sheets.

- Added the ability to double-click an Object reference to open that Object in Scriptable Sheets.

- Added a Batch Select context menu option to open or delete multiple Sheets at once from a single popup.

- Added a setting for Headers to always discard the first row on import regardless of column names matching.

- Google Sheets Importers can now target a specific folder so an importer only imports into the assets within that folder.

- The import button now shows a dropdown to choose between importers when more than one targets the selected type.

**Fixes**

- Fixed a crash when toggling Show Column Index during an import.

- Fixed import header row not being stripped when the column index was shown.

- Fixed an asset import worker warning when Auto Generate created Objects.

- Fixed delete not removing an auto generated Object directly after an import or paste.

**v1.10.1**

**Fixes**

- Fixed Collection Tables not rendering serialize reference elements.

- Added new serialize reference samples to validate fixes.

- Fixed the Collection Table dropdown staying active when switching to a type with no instances.

- Fixed the create button being hidden for a type with no instances after viewing a Collection Table.

- Fixed Collection Table sorting so the Index and field columns order the element rows within each group.

- Fixed noisy array element warnings when pasting into serialize reference fields with uneven array sizes.

- Fixed arrow key navigation getting stuck on empty cells.

- Fixed arrow key navigation not working properly with docked columns.

- Fixed arrow key navigation and click selection for Addressable Asset cells.

- Click selection on read-only cells now properly highlights the cell.

**v1.10.0**

**Features**

- Added Collection Tables to expand a single array or list field into a table of rows, grouped by Object.

- Google Sheets Importers can now target a specific collection table.

- Added Serialize Reference support to display columns for every concrete subtype with a per-row type dropdown.

- Added a Managed Type Columns option to the column header context menu to toggle which Serialize Reference subtype columns are shown.

- Added an Auto Generate setting to automatically create ScriptableObjects when importing or pasting more rows than exist.

- Property filters can now be chained together with & (and) and | (or) operators.

- Property filters can now reference columns by index using a $ prefix.

- Added settings to display the row and column index using spreadsheet style letters.

- Added an alphanumeric reference of the selected cell to the left of the search bar.

- The selected page is now saved and restored per Object type and sheet.

- The selected type is now remembered per Sheet Asset and restored when switching back.

- Added Ctrl/Cmd + Left/Right Arrow shortcuts to navigate between pages.

- Added a column header context menu option to set a custom header text color.

- Added a Paste Pad toolbar with various actions and rich text formatting options.

- Added a Paste Pad line number setting and a find/replace with a case sensitivity toggle.

- Added new Paste Pad Settings Window.

- Added an inline play button to preview AudioClips.

- Asset previews and thumbnails now display for Addressable Asset References.

- Added a Map Asset Preview option to the column header context menu to change asset previews.

- Added an Asset Preview Depth workload setting to control how deep the Map Asset Preview menu explores.

- Column header context menu actions now support undo/redo operations.

- Added a Hidden Sub Assets setting to include hidden sub-assets that aren't shown under their main asset.

**Fixes**

- Fixed the selected page resetting when entering play mode.

- Fixed property filters on the Name field for certain Prefab Components.

- Fixed missing script warnings logged while scanning hidden sub-assets.

- Improved table rendering performance and reduced per-frame allocations on large sheets.

- Improved search filtering performance.

**v1.9.1**

**Fixes**

- Fixed compiler errors in Unity 6.5 and warnings in Unity 6.4 caused by the deprecated GetInstanceID API.

- Fixed serialization analyzer warnings in Unity 6.5 for the settings and window session state types.

- Pasted and imported percentage values now parse into number fields instead of failing.

**v1.9.0**

**Features**

- New Best Fit setting that displays the maximum size of each array.

- Override Array Size is now enabled by default.

- Added buttons to add or remove elements from arrays.

- Added column header context menu items to hide, copy, or filter by the selected column.

- Added support for docking the Actions and Name columns via their context menus.

- Added scan settings to exclude specific folders and asset types.

- Search bar now expands based on the length of the search text.

**Fixes**

- Column header context menu now lists columns with the same name separately.

- Fixed an issue causing the column headers to grow with the row height.

- Fixed an issue with the column visibility popup horizontal scrollbar not appearing.

- Fixed a Unity warning that occurred when too many context menu items were present.

- Fixed an issue where showing the row index could cause the Actions column to overlap Name.

**v1.8.0**

**Features**

- ScriptableObject fields with no assigned asset now include an option to create and assign a new instance.

- Unity's Localization fields now show intuitive table and entry fields instead of raw IDs.

- Increased the max override size for arrays.

- Newly created Objects are now auto selected.

**Fixes**

- Fixed an issue where Google Sheets Importers ignored the visible columns setting.

Full changelog available [here](https://github.com/LunaWolfStudios/ScriptableSheetsDocs/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

items.title: Request for batch processing: Remove row export limits and support auto-generation of ScriptableObjects.
items.text:
I am writing to suggest improvements regarding the data export and import workflow.

Current issues:

Export Limit: The export function is restricted by the current Row Size (e.g., if the Row Size is set to 40, only 40 items are exported). This forces users to repeat the import/export process multiple times for large datasets, which is highly inefficient.

Missing Feature (Auto-generation): When importing a TSV or CSV file containing new data (e.g., adding 1,000 rows in Excel to a 10-row sample), the system does not automatically create the corresponding ScriptableObject assets for the new entries.

Requested Improvements:

Batch Export: Please allow all data to be exported at once, regardless of the Row Size setting in the inspector.

Auto-generation on Import: Please implement a feature where the tool automatically creates new ScriptableObject assets if the imported file contains rows that do not currently exist in the project.

Improving these features would significantly enhance the workflow for developers managing large-scale data.

publisherReply.text:
Thanks for the detailed review and thoughtful suggestions!

For batch export, this is actually already supported. Under Data Transfer settings you can disable “Page Rows Only” and “Visible Columns Only” to export all rows and columns regardless of what is currently shown in the table.

Auto generation of ScriptableObjects on import is now supported as of version 1.10.0 just enable "Auto Generation" under Object Management settings.

items.title: Very good but have some problems
items.text:
I think this asset is very good, but a couple of issues keep me from giving it 5 stars:

1- When working with big SOs, the inspector becomes extremely slow and hard to use.

2- Row and column limit (only 20 rows displayed at once with no way to increase it without causing performance bottlenecks). If you have 100+ ScriptableObjects, you constantly need to click through “Previous/Next” pages, which slows down workflow.

If these are improved, this would easily be a 5-star asset for me.

publisherReply.text:
Thank you for the review. Here are some tips that address your concerns!

You can increase the number of visible rows and columns under Workload Settings.

If you're trying to render 1000+ cells in full screen there will be a performance dip. Scriptable Sheets makes use of virtualization for rendering. So you can improve performance by reducing your window size or increasing the row line height.

My best recommendation though is to create and save different Sheet layouts. You can toggle on/off only the columns you need and save that layout. This not only makes it easier edit the data that matters the most to you, but it will also vastly improve performance even when 100 rows are displayed at once.

I would highly recommend watching the videos and reading the documentation for more performance tips.

items.title: Nice tool but can be even better!
items.text:
The asset definitely makes working with ScriptableObjects easier, but I’m still missing the functionality I was hoping for — the kind of feature that would make this a dream asset for me.

My game relies heavily on composed ScriptableObjects, meaning I create game entities from different parts (i.e., ScriptableObjects). The process of creating new child SOs is quite tedious: first, you need to create an SO by selecting the correct type from a long list, then you have to go to the parent and search for the newly created one to assign it as the parent SO’s property. This has to be done for every child SO.

In the Godot engine, for example, the same procedure is much easier. When you select a parent resource (similar to a ScriptableObject in Unity), you can create a new child directly within the parent, and you don’t even have to choose the type, since it only shows the one that is defined for this specific property. I really miss this functionality in Unity. If it’s possible to add this feature to the asset, that would be super awesome!

publisherReply.text: Thank you for the feedback! This feature has been added in v1.8.0. ScriptableObject fields with no assigned asset now include an option to create and assign a new instance.

items.title: A great Power Tool for ScriptableObject fans
items.text:
I use a lot of ScriptableObjects and they're basically data, so a spreadsheet format looks and feels like a big step forward.

I was a bit wary of all the bubbly reviews for this "Really amazing asset! ...etc." but I have 27 types of S.O. in my current project, varying from enum-like usages (a named object of a specific type so I get a nice drop-down in the inspector) up to one which has 20+ data members/fields and functions/methods built into it (and I currently have 96 instances of just that type in my project). This asset really helps manage them all.

After using repeatedly for a few days, it feels almost feature-complete. Some items like a variable-length list inside your S.O. just don't translate easily to column format and the author just shows you the first one by default [edit: this behavior can be changed in the settings! amazing]

Also, I'd written import/export (e.g. to CSV) tools for my own S.O's but this even has that, and probably does it better than mine.

Footnote: I also like that it's completely drop-in/out and doesn't need to move with my project if I share work (e.g. in game jams) with people who do not have a license. That offsets the slight frowny-face when I saw it's an "extension asset" which I understand requires one license per seat/user.

publisherReply.text:
I really appreciate the generous review! Thank you!

Edit: I wanted to add that starting in v1.10.0 support for arrays has been vastly improved with the addition of Collection Tables.

items.title: Handy asset with great support
items.text:
I've been looking for a way to manage my SO-heavy projects by writing my own editors and managers. This asset handles all of that in a simple and easy to work with format that is very recognizable to designers. 

On top of being a great asset that will find a use in most projects, the support has been great - with developers providing updates based on feedback. 

Keep it up!

publisherReply.text: I appreciate the feedback! It's encouraging to know that it's making a positive impact on your workflow with Scriptable Objects in Unity. Thanks for the support!

items.text: Does what it says it does and the developer is very responsive and open to improvements.

items.title: Literally game changing!
items.text: I am building out a TCG.  I keep all of my cards in spreadsheets so that I can immediately add cards as inspiration strikes.  However, previously I needed to copy and paste the values from Google Sheets into the Unity UI.  But now I can use this!  It lets me import for my first iteration of cards, and then it lets me look at a sheet view of all of my cards for making edits as I test things.  I can make bulk changes instantly here, where it would take me 15-30 minutes before.  This helps my development go faster, which is key for ensuring my game actually gets finished and published!

publisherReply.text: Thank you for the review! That’s great to hear how much time it’s saving you! Best of luck with your trading card game!

items.text: Scriptable sheets is an amazing way to clearly organize our assets in the engine. The import / export functionality is extremely helpful for games with large sets of assets, and it also helps how intuitive it is to use! Couldn't recommend it more!

publisherReply.text: Thanks so much for your wonderful review! We're thrilled to hear you're enjoying Scriptable Sheets and finding it helpful. Your recommendation means a lot to us!

decisionsForOrchestrator: Awards wording. The owner said "nominated", which matches the official record. Unity's own results page labels non-winning nominees "Runner-ups". Suggested public wording: "Nominee, Best Development Tool, 17th Unity Awards (2025)" and "Luna Wolf Studios: Nominee, Breakthrough Publisher, Unity Awards 2025". Do not say "winner" or "finalist". "Runner-up" is also accurate per Unity's wording, but could read as second place; the orchestrator should pick one term.

Category name. The nominee list and results say "Breakthrough Publisher"; the awards FAQ category list calls the same award "Breakthrough Asset Award*". Use "Breakthrough Publisher" (the name on the published results).

Badge. Ask the owner for the official digital nominee badge Unity sent. Do not recreate a Unity laurel. Section 12 title/logo rights are for winners only; showing the nominee badge is covered only by the section 9 line about sharing it on "storefronts and socials".

Surname. Kodeco credits "Jeff [the page prints his surname]" and the Kodeco URLs contain no name, but CLAUDE.md says Jeff goes by first name only on the site. Link the tutorials without printing the surname, or get the owner's OK.

Kodeco credit accuracy. The ScriptableObject tutorial is now bylined Ben MacKinnon ("Original post by Jeff [the page prints his surname]"), and the Tower Defense Part 1 tutorial was an update of Barbara Reichart's original. Describe them as "original author" and "updated" respectively, not as sole authorship.

Reviews. The old site edited two quotes (Katerlad and RestingOwl merge the review title into the body; Quevanto and RestingOwl drop sentences without marks). CLAUDE.md requires exact reproduction: use the verbatim title and body from this file, or mark cuts with an ellipsis.

Rating display. Unity stores the average as 5 (rounded) but the publisher page shows 4.9 (31 five-star + 3 four-star = 4.91). Say "4.9 out of 5 from 34 reviews" or "34 reviews, 31 of them five-star"; avoid "5 stars".
Price. $24.99 is a sale price on the access date. Show the regular $49.99, or no price, and link to the listing for the current price.

Unity version wording. The listing says "Supports Unity LTS versions 2020.3 and up"; the listing's "Original Unity version" is 2022.3.62 (Unity does not say what this field means beyond its label). Use the 2020.3+ claim, citing the listing.
